name: short paragraph, untouched
text: This is a short paragraph that needs no splitting at all.

name: two sentences over the limit
text: The first sentence is here. The second sentence follows it.

name: ordinary prose
text: This is a test that depend on the underlying architecture of this software, it mays work or not, depending on the processor. A second sentence follows here and it is also of a reasonable length. A third one, shorter. And a fourth to push it over the limit so the splitting has work to do.

name: one very long sentence
text: This single sentence runs on and on without any terminal punctuation at all so it cannot be divided at a sentence boundary and must go out as it is

name: question and exclamation marks
text: Is this a question? It certainly is! And this one ends with a full stop. Another here.

name: quotes after the full stop
text: He said "this is the first part." Then she replied "and this is the second." Done.

name: ellipsis as a terminator
text: It trailed off here… And then resumed properly. A third sentence closes it.

name: leading and trailing space
text: A paragraph padded with blank space on both sides.

name: abbreviations, the classic trap
text: We met Dr. Smith on Tuesday. He works at the U.S. embassy in Rome. It was brief.

name: decimal numbers
text: The value was 3.14 and the other was 2.71 exactly. That is the whole result.

name: limit below the floor
text: The floor is one hundred and twenty characters, so a smaller limit is raised to it rather than producing a chunk per word.

name: an abbreviation exactly at a packing boundary
text: The report was prepared in Washington. It covers the whole of the U.S. market for the year, including every region. A closing sentence rounds it off nicely.
